title: Zapier vs Make: Automation Workflow Fit
description: Compare Zapier and Make for integration coverage, workflow complexity, debugging, reliability, governance, and total automation cost. Current plan limits and prices are not independently verified here; validate them for your task volume.

features.name: Workflow design
features.tool1: Automation builder for connected app workflows
features.tool1Detail: Prototype a real workflow with triggers, filters, branching, retries, and clear ownership; confirm which steps are supported on your intended plan.
features.tool2Detail: Prototype the same workflow and assess how its branching, transformations, routers, and error paths are represented and maintained.

features.name: Integration coverage
features.tool1Detail: Verify the exact apps, events, actions, authentication methods, and required fields; connector availability alone does not prove the full workflow is supported.
features.tool2Detail: Verify the exact modules, events, API operations, authentication, and field mapping needed for your workflow.

features.name: Complex data handling
features.tool1Detail: Test pagination, arrays, missing fields, deduplication, rate limits, and payload sizes using realistic records.
features.tool2Detail: Test nested data, arrays, conditional routes, aggregation, missing values, and payload limits using realistic records.

features.name: Reliability and recovery
features.tool1: Run history, alerts, retries, and failure handling
features.tool1Detail: Simulate expired credentials, API throttling, duplicate events, and downstream outages; verify logs, replay behavior, and alert ownership.
features.tool2Detail: Simulate API errors, rate limits, partial failures, and duplicate events; confirm how execution details, retries, and recovery are handled.

features.name: Governance and maintenance
features.tool1Detail: Check team access, shared ownership, environment separation, change review, and documentation for business-critical automations.
features.tool2Detail: Check access, ownership, documentation, change management, and how the team audits and maintains scenarios over time.

features.name: Pricing and total cost
features.tool1Detail: Confirm current plan pricing, included tasks, premium app rules, polling behavior, and overage or upgrade conditions directly with Zapier.
features.tool2Detail: Confirm current plan pricing, operation or credit accounting, execution limits, scheduling, and overage or upgrade conditions directly with Make.

verdict: Zapier and Make both automate workflows between services, but the best fit depends on the exact connector coverage, workflow complexity, debugging experience, reliability requirements, team governance, and pricing model. Build the same end-to-end automation in both tools, run representative volume, and include maintenance and failure recovery in the evaluation. The legacy score, winner, and price ranges are not independently verified here, so this page does not declare a universal winner.

faqs.question: Is Zapier better than Make?
faqs.answer: Not universally. Compare both using your actual apps and workflow, then evaluate reliability, maintainability, debugging, and total cost at realistic usage.

faqs.question: Which is cheaper for automation?
faqs.answer: The answer depends on the current plans, task or operation accounting, frequency, premium connectors, and volume. Estimate usage from a real workflow and confirm current vendor terms before deciding.

faqs.question: What should I test in a pilot?
faqs.answer: Test authentication expiry, API rate limits, duplicate events, missing data, branching, retries, alerting, run history, ownership, and recovery from downstream outages.

faqs.question: Are the scores and winner on this page independently verified?
faqs.answer: No. The old numerical ratings, winner, and price ranges are not presented as verified evidence. Use the workflow-fit criteria and confirm current product details directly with each vendor.

faqs.question: What should I test before choosing Zapier or Make?
faqs.answer: Build the same automation in both tools and test authentication expiry, rate limits, duplicate events, missing data, retries, alerts, logs, ownership, and recovery from downstream outages.
